claim: Wnt4 expression is first observed in cells at the tip-stalk junction that represent PTA structures prior to epithelialisation.
source: Wnt4 expression was first observed in cells at the tip-stalk junction that represent PTA structures prior to epithelialisation.
evidence: Based on correlation of Wnt4-GFP expression with aPKC staining patterns that define stages of nephron formation.

claim: Wnt4 expression is maintained into the primitive and maturing renal vesicle.
source: Expression was maintained into the primitive and maturing RV (Figure 1a–c).
evidence: Supported by imaging data showing Wnt4-GFP expression in primitive and mature RV structures.

claim: GFP signal was not observed within nephron progenitor cells on top of the tip.
source: GFP signal was not observed within nephron progenitor cells on top of the tip.
evidence: Based on imaging of Wnt4-GFP expression patterns.

claim: Wnt4-GFP is evident at lower levels in some stromal cells, particularly in the medulla, consistent with previous reports.
source: Wnt4-GFP was evident at lower levels in some stromal cells, particularly in the medulla, consistent with previous reports (Georgas et al., 2008; Itäranta et al., 2006) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by imaging data and cited previous studies.

claim: At E13.5, 24 hr after tamoxifen treatment, tdTomato-labelled Wnt4 lineage cells were restricted to regions of Wnt4-GFP expression in the PTA and RV structures.
source: At E13.5, 24 hr after tamoxifen treatment, tdTomato-labelled Wnt4 lineage cells were restricted to regions of Wnt4-GFP expression in the PTA and RV structures, as anticipated for committing cells (Figure 1g–k).
evidence: Based on lineage tracing experiments with imaging at 24 hr post-tamoxifen.

claim: At E14.5 and E15.5, tdTomato-labelled SIX2+ cells were identified within the cap mesenchyme.
source: At E14.5 and E15.5, 48 and 72 hr after tamoxifen treatment, tdTomato labelling was observed within developing nephrons as a result of earlier labelling in precursor structures (Figure 1l–u). However, we also identified tdTomato-labelled SIX2+ cells within the cap mesenchyme.
evidence: Based on lineage tracing experiments with imaging at 48 and 72 hr post-tamoxifen.

claim: Wnt4-lineage progenitors appeared as single cells or small groups of cells in some but not all cap domains at E14.5.
source: These appeared as single cells or small groups of cells in some but not all cap domains at E14.5 (Figure 1l–p).
evidence: Based on imaging data at E14.5.

claim: Some cap domains at E15.5 contained clusters of tdTomato-labelled cells expressing SIX2 but not Wnt4-GFP.
source: Such Wnt4-lineage progenitors were more apparent at E15.5 with some cap domains containing clusters of tdTomato-labelled cells expressing SIX2 but not Wnt4-GFP (Figure 1q–u, Video 1), suggesting that they were labelled as a result of previous Wnt4 expression in a PTA rather than induction of differentiation in individual cells away from the site of nephron formation.
evidence: Based on imaging data at E15.5 showing SIX2+tdTomato+ cells without Wnt4-GFP expression.

claim: Lineage tracing with an inducible Pdgfra Cre results in extensive stromal labelling but does not result in labelled cells within the cap mesenchyme.
source: Using this line results in extensive stromal labelling but does not result in labelled cells within the cap mesenchyme (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on lineage tracing experiments using PdgfraCreER.

claim: Wnt4-lineage contributions to the nephron progenitor population arise from the established sites of Wnt4 expression in the early committing nephron, not from the stroma.
source: As such, Wnt4-lineage contributions to the nephron progenitor population arise from the established sites of Wnt4 expression in the early committing nephron, not from the stroma.
evidence: Based on comparison of Wnt4-Cre and Pdgfra-Cre lineage tracing results.

claim: Labelled nephron progenitor cells arise from a portion of the committing population that 'escape' commitment and re-enter the cap mesenchyme over time.
source: We hypothesised that labelled nephron progenitor cells arise from a portion of the committing population that 'escape' commitment and re-enter the cap mesenchyme over time.
evidence: Based on the observation of Wnt4-lineage cells in the cap mesenchyme at later timepoints.

claim: Wnt4-lineage cells were observed in the cap mesenchyme at E19.5, seven days after labelling at E12.5.
source: To test whether these cells were able to self-renew long term, or were prone to differentiation, we labelled at E12.5 and assessed developing kidneys seven days later at E19.5. Wnt4-lineage cells were observed in the cap mesenchyme of these samples suggesting that they return to an uninduced progenitor state (Figure 2a).
evidence: Based on lineage tracing with 7-day chase period.

claim: Labelling at E14.5 reveals cap re-entry later in development, with labelled cells absent from the SIX2 positive cap domain at E15.5, but a small number of cells present at E16.5 and E17.5.
source: Labelling at E14.5 reveals cap re-entry later in development, with labelled cells absent from the SIX2 positive cap domain at E15.5, but a small number of cells present at E16.5 and E17.5.
evidence: Based on lineage tracing experiments initiated at E14.5.

claim: Re-entry of Wnt4-lineage cells does not appear to be restricted to early kidney development.
source: Thus, re-entry of Wnt4-lineage cells does not appear to be restricted to early kidney development.
evidence: Based on observation of cap re-entry at multiple developmental stages.

claim: tdTomato labelling within the nephron lineage was restricted to sites of nephron commitment throughout development.
source: We confirmed that tdTomato labelling within the nephron lineage was restricted to sites of nephron commitment throughout development by examining embryos 24 hr after injection at E12.5, E14.5 and E16.5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on 24 hr chase experiments at multiple developmental stages.

claim: Wnt4-GFP expression was not detected outside the tip-stalk junction at any stage.
source: Wnt4-GFP expression was not detected outside the tip-stalk junction at any stage.
evidence: Based on imaging data across developmental stages.

claim: tdTomato-labelled nephron progenitor cells must be derived from cells within the site of nephron formation that have re-entered the nephron progenitor pool over time.
source: Thus, tdTomato-labelled nephron progenitor cells must be derived from cells within the site of nephron formation that have re-entered the nephron progenitor pool over time.
evidence: Based on the restriction of Wnt4-GFP expression to the tip-stalk junction and the presence of tdTomato+ cells in the cap.

claim: Analysis of SIX2 and Wnt4-GFP expression within tdTomato+ cells revealed a shift from a SIX2+Wnt4-GFP+tdTomato+ state to a SIX2+tdTomato+ population over time.
source: This is supported by analysis of SIX2 and Wnt4-GFP expression within tdTomato +cells in our imaging data, which revealed a shift from a SIX2+Wnt4-GFP+tdTomato+ state (cells were located at the tip-stalk junction), to a SIX2+tdTomato+ population over time (Figure 2c, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Based on quantitative image analysis of marker expression in tdTomato+ cells.

claim: Labelled cells expressing both SIX2 and Wnt4-GFP were observed around the base of the ureteric bud at E11.5 after labelling at E10.5.
source: Labelled cells expressing both SIX2 and Wnt4-GFP were observed around the base of the ureteric bud at E11.5.
evidence: Based on lineage tracing initiated at E10.5 and examined at E11.5.

claim: The majority of cells labelled at E10.5 contributed to nephrons while some labelled cells reintegrated into the cap mesenchyme.
source: The majority of these cells contributed to nephrons while some labelled cells reintegrated into the cap mesenchyme (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Based on lineage tracing from E10.5.

claim: Some tdTomato-labelled cells remained within Wnt4-GFP+ PTA-like regions 72 hr after labelling at E10.5.
source: Some tdTomato-labelled cells remained within Wnt4-GFP+ PTA-like regions 72 hr after labelling (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Based on imaging 72 hr after E10.5 labelling.

claim: While some cells may initiate Wnt4 expression and then subsequently re-enter the cap mesenchyme, others remain at sites of induction without immediately progressing to epithelialization.
source: Hence, while some cells may initiate Wnt4 expression and then subsequently re-enter the cap mesenchyme, others remain at sites of induction without immediately progressing to epithelialization.
evidence: Based on observation of cells remaining in Wnt4-GFP+ regions without progressing to RV.

claim: By E17.5, labelled cells within or near early committing structures appear to be restricted to niches with highly labelled nephron progenitor populations.
source: In contrast, by E17.5, labelled cells within or near early committing structures appear to be restricted to niches with highly labelled nephron progenitor populations, suggesting that these cells arise from new inductions of previously labelled cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Based on imaging at E17.5 after E10.5 labelling.

claim: While cells that remain induced may not immediately progress to a more mature nephron stage, such cells appear to ultimately commit.
source: Thus, while cells that remain induced may not immediately progress to a more mature nephron stage, such cells appear to ultimately commit.
evidence: Based on the observation that cells remaining at induction sites eventually contribute to nephrons.

claim: Using a constitutive Wnt4-GFP-Cre line, frequent cap labelling (~20–30% of SIX2+ cells) was observed at E18.5.
source: Frequent cap labelling (~20–30% of SIX2+ cells, Figure 2h) was observed at E18.5 using the constitutive Wnt4-Cre line, confirming that Wnt4-lineage'escapers' accumulate in the cap mesenchyme throughout development, and ultimately represent a considerable proportion of the nephron progenitor population (Figure 2g,h).
evidence: Based on lineage tracing with constitutive Wnt4-Cre.

claim: A portion of the cap remained unlabelled with constitutive Wnt4-Cre, suggesting that not all nephron progenitor cells arise from cells that have expressed Wnt4 during the time period examined.
source: Nonetheless, a portion of the cap remained unlabelled suggesting that not all nephron progenitor cells arise from cells that have expressed Wnt4 during the time period examined.
evidence: Based on quantification of constitutive Wnt4-Cre labelling.

claim: Some Wnt4-lineage cells moved from the region under the tip to the top or end of a tip during live imaging.
source: Live imaging E12.5 samples for 24 hr showed some Wnt4-lineage cells moving from the region under the tip to the top or end of a tip (Figure 3g,j, Video 2).
evidence: Based on time-lapse imaging of Wnt4-lineage labelled cells.

claim: Fixed analysis after live imaging shows that tdTomato-labelled cells have migrated back into the cap mesenchyme and are surrounded by unlabelled SIX2-expressing cells.
source: Fixed analysis of these samples after live imaging shows that the tdTomato-labelled cells have migrated back into the cap mesenchyme and are surrounded by unlabelled SIX2-expressing cells (Figure 3h,i,k,l, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence analysis of samples after live imaging.

claim: The region under the tip that cells migrated from contains a population of cells that have more prominent basolateral localisation of NCAM and lower levels of SIX2, suggesting those cells are undergoing the early stages of epithelialisation.
source: The region under the tip that these cells migrated from contains a population of cells that have more prominent basolateral localisation of NCAM and lower levels of SIX2, suggesting those cells are undergoing the early stages of epithelialisation to form a nephron (Figure 3h,k).
evidence: Based on NCAM and SIX2 staining patterns in fixed samples after live imaging.

claim: Wnt4-lineage cells displayed a small increase in mean migration speed compared to Six2GCE labelled progenitors.
source: Comparing corrected migration speeds revealed that Wnt4-lineage cells displayed a small increase in mean migration speed compared to Six2GCE labelled progenitors (p<0.05, mixed effects model).
evidence: Based on quantitative analysis of cell tracking data comparing Wnt4-lineage and Six2-lineage cells.

claim: The increased migration speed of Wnt4-lineage cells may reflect a requirement for larger movements to achieve cap re-entry.
source: This may reflect a requirement for larger movements to achieve cap re-entry.
evidence: Interpretation of the observed increase in migration speed.

claim: The computational model predicts that labelling progenitor cells as they received an inductive signal gave rise to committed cells as well as cells that moved back out of the induction zone before reaching the threshold for commitment.
source: The model predicted that labelling progenitor cells as they received an inductive signal gave rise to committed cells as well as cells that moved back out of the induction zone before reaching the threshold for commitment (Figure 4c,d).
evidence: Based on computational simulation results.

claim: The in silico model supports the experimental finding that Wnt4-Cre labels both committing cells and a proportion of the nephron progenitor population.
source: Thus, the in silico model supports our experimental finding that Wnt4-Cre labels both committing cells and a proportion of the nephron progenitor population.
evidence: Based on agreement between computational model predictions and experimental observations.

claim: In the 'primed' model, as more cells accumulate inductive events the proportion of uninduced progenitors decreases with time.
source: In this scenario, as more cells accumulate inductive events the proportion of uninduced progenitors decreases with time (Figure 4g).
evidence: Based on computational simulation of the 'primed' model.

claim: The 'return to ground' model gave rise to a more sharply defined domain of cells that have recently undergone induction, where the proportion of uncommitted cells remained steady for a given niche size.
source: This scenario gave rise to a more sharply defined domain of cells that have recently undergone induction, where the proportion of uncommitted cells remained steady for a given niche size (Figure 4e,f,g).
evidence: Based on computational simulation of the 'return to ground' model.

claim: In both simulations, decreasing niche size or increasing the rate of random cell movement resulted in an increased proportion of induced cells.
source: In both simulations, decreasing niche size or increasing the rate of random cell movement resulted in an increased proportion of induced cells because cells were more likely to move into the induction zone (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Based on computational simulations with varying parameters.

claim: In the primed scenario the proportion of uninduced progenitors dropped sharply as niche size decreased, or migration rate increased leading to a collapse of the uncommitted population.
source: In the primed scenario the proportion of uninduced progenitors dropped sharply as niche size decreased, or migration rate increased leading to a collapse of the uncommitted population (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Based on computational simulation results for the 'primed' model.

claim: Changing niche size or migration rate in the 'return to ground' model resulted in a stepped decrease in the proportion of uninduced progenitors but reached equilibrium due to the capacity of induced progenitors to revert to an uninduced state.
source: Changing niche size or migration rate in the 'return to ground' model resulted in a stepped decrease in the proportion of uninduced progenitors but reached equilibrium due to the capacity of induced progenitors to revert to an uninduced state (Figure 4g,h).
evidence: Based on computational simulation results for the 'return to ground' model.

claim: Both computational models result in regionalized enrichment of uncommitted and induced progenitors.
source: Both models result in regionalized enrichment of uncommitted and induced progenitors.
evidence: Based on computational simulation results.

claim: In both the 'primed' and 'return to ground' scenarios, cells that were labelled as they received an inductive cue gave rise to both committed cells and 'escapers' in the progenitor pool.
source: In both the original 'primed' scenario and the 'return to ground' scenario, cells that were labelled as they received an inductive cue gave rise to both committed cells and 'escapers' in the progenitor pool (Figure 4c–f).
evidence: Based on computational simulation results.

claim: 27/42 labelled cells in single cell RNA-seq expressed both Six2 and tdTomato, but not Wnt4.
source: 27/42 labelled cells expressed both Six2 and tdTomato, but not Wnt4 suggesting that they represent the Wnt4 labelled nephron progenitor (escaper) population (Figure 5c,d).
evidence: Based on single cell RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: There was no evidence for significant differential expression between labelled cells and unlabelled cells within progenitor clusters.
source: There was no evidence for significant differential expression between labelled cells and unlabelled cells within progenitor clusters (average log fold change threshold 0.25).
evidence: Based on differential expression analysis of single cell RNA-seq data.

claim: The existence of Wnt4 lineage cells with a transcriptional profile identical to surrounding nephron progenitors most closely supports the 'return to ground' state computational model.
source: The existence of Wnt4 lineage cells with a transcriptional profile identical to surrounding nephron progenitors most closely supports our 'return to ground' state computational model, whereby cap re-entry allows cells to return to an uninduced progenitor state.
evidence: Based on comparison of single cell RNA-seq results with computational model predictions.

claim: tdTomato expressing cells were found within all nephron progenitor subpopulations, suggesting that previous expression of Wnt4 does not give rise to a distinct nephron progenitor state.
source: Similarly, tdTomato expressing cells were found within all nephron progenitor subpopulations, suggesting that previous expression of Wnt4 does not give rise to a distinct nephron progenitor state.
evidence: Based on distribution of tdTomato+ cells across nephron progenitor clusters in single cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Within the Wnt4-lineage-labelled nephron progenitor population, there was transcriptional heterogeneity with some cells showing a strong progenitor profile, while others appeared in a partially induced state.
source: Within the Wnt4-lineage-labelled nephron progenitor population, there was transcriptional heterogeneity. Some cells showed a strong progenitor profile, while others appeared in a partially induced state with co-expression of genes previously regarded as delineating progenitor and committed states (Figure 5d).
evidence: Based on hierarchical clustering and gene expression analysis of Wnt4-lineage cells in single cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Cells from initial Wnt4-labelled aggregates at E11.5 were motile and contributed to several adjacent nephrons.
source: Clusters of Wnt4-lineage cells at sites of nephron induction were imaged in E11.5 explants over 44 hr. Cells from these initial aggregates were motile and contributed to several adjacent nephrons, counter to the established understanding that a single induction event gives rise to a single nephron (Figure 6a, Video 4).
evidence: Based on time-lapse imaging of E11.5 explants.

claim: Wnt4-expressing cells labelled at E11.5 contributed to the majority of nephrons over time.
source: At the completion of live imaging explants were fixed and stained for JAG1, a marker of early nephrons, revealing that Wnt4-expressing cells labelled at E11.5 contributed to the majority of nephrons over time (Figure 6a).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence analysis after live imaging.

claim: Groups of Wnt4 lineage cells that were within 1–3 cell diameters of each other at the onset of imaging ultimately contributed to multiple adjacent nephrons.
source: Groups of Wnt4 lineage cells that were within 1–3 cell diameters of each other at the onset of imaging ultimately contributed to multiple adjacent nephrons (Figure 6b–k).
evidence: Based on cell tracking and post-imaging immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Progenitors in the early developing kidney are able to commit via a delayed process whereby a group of motile induced progenitors can give rise to multiple nephrons over the proceeding branching iterations.
source: Thus progenitors in the early developing kidney are able to commit via a delayed process whereby a group of motile induced progenitors can give rise to multiple nephrons over the proceeding branching iterations.
evidence: Based on live imaging observations of Wnt4-labelled cells contributing to multiple nephrons.

claim: The fact that cells have both initiated Wnt4 expression and remain in a region where they should be able to receive a positional inductive event implies that additional events downstream of WNT9B secretion and Wnt4 expression are required for nephron initiation.
source: The fact that such cells have both initiated Wnt4 expression and remain in a region in which they should be able to receive a positional inductive event implies that additional events downstream of WNT9B secretion and Wnt4 expression are required for nephron initiation.
evidence: Based on the observation that Wnt4-expressing cells can remain motile and not immediately commit.

claim: It is currently unclear whether induced progenitors undergo delayed commitment or contribute to more than one nephron at later stages of kidney development when niches are smaller and more discrete.
source: It is currently unclear whether induced progenitors undergo delayed commitment or contribute to more than one nephron at later stages of kidney development when niches are smaller and more discrete.
evidence: Acknowledgment of limitation in current understanding.

claim: Nephron progenitor commitment is a stochastic process influenced by cell migration.
source: Nephron progenitor commitment is a stochastic process influenced by cell migration
evidence: This is the title of the manuscript and represents the central claim supported by multiple lines of evidence throughout the study.

claim: Nephron progenitor cells can traverse the transcriptional hierarchy between self-renewal and commitment in either direction.
source: Single cell RNA-seq and computational modelling of returning cells reveals that nephron progenitors can traverse the transcriptional hierarchy between self-renewal and commitment in either direction.
evidence: Based on single cell RNA-seq showing Wnt4-lineage cells with progenitor transcriptional profiles and computational modeling.

claim: This plasticity may enable robust regulation of nephrogenesis as niches remodel and grow during organogenesis.
source: This plasticity may enable robust regulation of nephrogenesis as niches remodel and grow during organogenesis.
evidence: Interpretation of the functional significance of observed plasticity.

claim: Nephron progenitor cells surround the tips of the ureteric epithelium forming a 'cap mesenchyme' domain that is embedded within, but distinct from cortical stroma and vasculature.
source: Nephron progenitor cells surround the tips of the ureteric epithelium forming a 'cap mesenchyme' domain that is embedded within, but distinct from cortical stroma and vasculature.
evidence: Description of established anatomical organization.

claim: The least committed nephron progenitor cells are at the 'top' of the tip and nephron formation occurs at the 'bottom', in the junction between tip and stalk of the ureteric epithelium.
source: Together these populations form the nephrogenic niche, with the least committed nephron progenitor cells at the 'top' of the tip and nephron formation occurring at the 'bottom', in the junction between tip and stalk of the ureteric epithelium (Mugford et al., 2009).
evidence: Description of established spatial organization with citation.

claim: Tips produce WNT11, BMP7, FGF9 and WNT9B, which act to maintain progenitor self-renewal and survival.
source: Tips produce WNT11, BMP7, FGF9 and WNT9B, which act to maintain progenitor self-renewal and survival (Barak et al., 2012; Brown et al., 2013; Karner et al., 2011; Majumdar et al., 2003).
evidence: Statement of established signaling factors with citations.

claim: Canonical Wnt signalling, involving WNT9B from the ureteric epithelium, is critical to induce the epithelialisation of nephron progenitor cells to form nephrons.
source: Canonical Wnt signalling, involving WNT9B from the ureteric epithelium, is critical to induce the epithelialisation of nephron progenitor cells to form nephrons (Carroll et al., 2005; Karner et al., 2011; Park et al., 2007; Ramalingam et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement of established signaling mechanism with citations.

claim: Cells close to the tip-stalk junction receive higher levels of WNT9B and initiate commitment by upregulating genes required for nephron initiation such as Wnt4.
source: The prevailing model of nephron progenitor differentiation is that cells close to the tip-stalk junction receive higher levels of WNT9B and initiate commitment by upregulating further genes required for nephron initiation such as Wnt4 (Kispert et al., 1998; Stark et al., 1994).
evidence: Description of prevailing model with citations.

claim: Prior to epithelialisation, nephron progenitors coalesce to form a pretubular aggregate (PTA), which is characterised as a cluster of cells in the tip-stalk junction, defined by expression of Wnt4, Fgf8, Pax8, and Lhx1.
source: Prior to epithelialisation, nephron progenitors coalesce to form a pretubular aggregate (PTA), which is characterised as a cluster of cells in the tip-stalk junction, defined by expression of Wnt4, Fgf8, Pax8, and Lhx1 (Carroll et al., 2005; Georgas et al., 2009; Stark et al., 1994).
evidence: Description of established developmental stage with citations.

claim: PTAs are groups of cells within the tip-stalk junction that do not have a lumen or defined apical-basal polarity.
source: Detailed studies of cell polarity and lumen formation in the early nephron identify PTAs as groups of cells within the tip-stalk junction that do not have a lumen or defined apical-basal polarity (Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: Description of PTA characteristics with citation.

claim: Cells within the PTA transition to a primitive renal vesicle (RV), defined as having one or two apical foci containing polarity proteins such as aPKC and PAR3.
source: Cells within the PTA transition to a primitive renal vesicle (RV), defined as having one or two apical foci containing polarity proteins such as aPKC and PAR3.
evidence: Description of developmental transition with reference to polarity markers.

claim: Apical foci in primitive RV connect to form a single continuous lumen in a mature renal vesicle, which now represents an epithelium.
source: These foci connect to form a single continuous lumen in a mature renal vesicle, which now represents an epithelium (Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: Description of epithelialization process with citation.

claim: Clonal lineage tracing of nephron progenitor cells suggests that one sibling can remain in the progenitor domain while another contributes to a nephron.
source: Clonal lineage tracing of nephron progenitor cells suggests that one sibling can remain in the progenitor domain while another contributes to a nephron (Kobayashi et al., 2008).
evidence: Statement of previous lineage tracing results with citation.

claim: Live imaging of 852 individual nephron progenitor cells over 18 hr revealed substantial cell migration within the cap mesenchyme.
source: Counter to this model, our own live imaging of 852 individual nephron progenitor cells over 18 hr revealed substantial cell migration within the cap mesenchyme (Combes et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement of previous live imaging results with citation.

claim: Nephron progenitor cells moved randomly within and between niches, with this movement influenced by attraction, repulsion, and adhesion to the ureteric tip.
source: Nephron progenitor cells moved randomly within and between niches, with this movement influenced by attraction, repulsion, and adhesion to the ureteric tip.
evidence: Description of cell migration behavior from previous work.

claim: Some cells made large movements from the 'self-renewing' to the 'committing' region and vice versa, potentially crossing previously proposed domain boundaries.
source: Far from a population gradually transitioning through static subdomains, some cells made large movements from the 'self-renewing' to the 'committing' region and vice versa, potentially crossing previously proposed domain boundaries (Combes et al., 2016).
evidence: Description of cell migration patterns from previous work.

claim: Nephron progenitor cell fate is dependent on the duration of exposure to spatially-restricted inductive cues, with this being influenced by random cell migration.
source: Based on timelapse imaging, computational modelling, and scRNA-seq, we propose a refined model of nephron progenitor commitment in which cell fate is dependent on the duration of exposure to spatially-restricted inductive cues, with this being influenced by random cell migration.
evidence: Summary of the proposed model based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: This model predicts that Wnt4 expressing cells in the lower cap are in a plastic state.
source: This model predicts that Wnt4 expressing cells in the lower cap are in a plastic state.
evidence: Prediction from the proposed model.

claim: Depending on the duration of exposure, Wnt4-expressing cells may either commit to forming a nephron or re-enter the progenitor pool.
source: Depending on the duration of exposure they may either commit to forming a nephron or re-enter the progenitor pool.
evidence: Prediction from the proposed model.

claim: A population of swarming progenitors gives rise to a constant pool of committing cells.
source: Under this model, a population of swarming progenitors gives rise to a constant pool of committing cells.
evidence: Description of model behavior.

claim: The ability to undergo cap re-entry is quickly lost as cells aggregate.
source: Given that most cells within the PTA region go on to form nephrons we predict that the ability to undergo cap re-entry is quickly lost as cells aggregate.
evidence: Prediction based on observed behavior of PTA cells.

claim: Re-entry events may be restricted to cells that are excluded as an aggregate forms.
source: Thus, re-entry events may be restricted to cells that are excluded as an aggregate forms.
evidence: Speculation about the mechanism of cap re-entry.

claim: The fate of progenitors in the tip-stalk junction depends on migration events that occur immediately prior to the switch to a non-motile state.
source: This is consistent with our model, whereby the fate of progenitors in the tip-stalk junction depends on migration events that occur immediately prior to the switch to a non-motile state.
evidence: Interpretation consistent with the proposed model.

claim: The WNT9B-mediated induction of Wnt4 has been regarded as essential for commitment of SIX2+ nephron progenitor cells to nephron formation for more than a decade.
source: The WNT9B-mediated induction of Wnt4 has been regarded as essential for commitment of SIX2+nephron progenitor cells to nephron formation for more than a decade (Carroll et al., 2005; Kispert et al., 1998; Park et al., 2012; Park et al., 2007; Stark et al., 1994).
evidence: Statement of established understanding with citations.

claim: Phosphorylated SMAD1/5-mediated BMP signalling has been identified as a factor required to transition nephron progenitor cells into a state where they are receptive to inductive cues.
source: Phosphorylated SMAD1/5-mediated BMP signalling has been identified as a factor required to transition nephron progenitor cells into a state where they are receptive to inductive cues (Brown et al., 2013).
evidence: Statement of previous finding with citation.

claim: Recent studies suggest a capacity for Notch activation to induce nephron commitment.
source: Recent studies would suggest a capacity for Notch activation to induce nephron commitment (Chung et al., 2016; Chung et al., 2017), consistent with the commitment of all nephron progenitors after targeted activation of Notch signalling within the cap mesenchyme (Boyle et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement of recent findings with citations.

claim: The observation of cells which receive a trigger to initiate Wnt4 expression but fail to commit may indicate a requirement for prolonged induction or a second, as yet undefined, consolidating trigger.
source: Our observation of cells which receive a trigger to initiate Wnt4 expression but fail to commit may indicate a requirement for prolonged induction or a second, as yet undefined, consolidating trigger.
evidence: Interpretation of the observation that some Wnt4-expressing cells do not commit.

claim: Lineage tracing using a later marker of commitment (eg Jag1, Lhx1) would not give rise to cells that re-enter the nephron progenitor population.
source: These data predict that lineage tracing using a later marker of commitment (eg Jag1, Lhx1) would not give rise to cells that re-enter the nephron progenitor population.
evidence: Prediction based on the proposed model and observations.

claim: Previous heterochronic transplantation studies have suggested that there is a transcriptional signature related to cap mesenchyme 'aging' but that placing an 'old' nephron progenitor back within a 'young' niche extended the time across which this cell would remain a nephron progenitor.
source: Previous heterochronic transplantation studies have suggested that there is a transcriptional signature related to cap mesenchyme 'aging' but that placing an 'old' nephron progenitor back within a 'young' niche extended the time across which this cell would remain a nephron progenitor (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement of previous findings with citation.

claim: There was no evidence for differential expression of markers associated with nephron progenitor aging in Wnt4-Cre-labelled vs unlabelled progenitors.
source: We found no evidence for differential expression of markers associated with nephron progenitor aging in Wnt4-Cre-labelled vs unlabelled progenitors.
evidence: Based on analysis of single cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Individual nephron progenitor cell fate depends on migration events that modulate exposure to niche cues, yet the nephron progenitor population as a whole reaches an equilibrium for a given set of values.
source: In our 'return to ground state' model, individual nephron progenitor cell fate depends on migration events that modulate exposure to niche cues, yet the nephron progenitor population as a whole reaches an equilibrium for a given set of values.
evidence: Description of model behavior.

claim: Cells from an older population with a greater proportion of induced cells may adjust to match the equilibrium of a 'young' niche state given appropriate instructive cues.
source: Thus, in our paradigm, cells from an older population with a greater proportion of induced cells may adjust to match the equilibrium of a 'young' niche state given appropriate instructive cues.
evidence: Interpretation of model behavior in context of previous heterochronic transplantation studies.

claim: Computational simulations of the stochastic model are consistent with eventual cessation of nephrogenesis.
source: Computational simulations of our stochastic model are consistent with eventual cessation of nephrogenesis.
evidence: Based on computational simulation results.

claim: A reduction in niche size shifts the equilibrium toward a more primed population as cells spend more time in zones of induction and less time in receipt of tip signals promoting progenitor maintenance.
source: We propose that the duration of inductive signal required for commitment could remain steady, with a reduction in niche size shifting the equilibrium toward a more primed population as cells spend more time in zones of induction and less time in receipt of tip signals promoting progenitor maintenance.
evidence: Interpretation of model behavior and proposed mechanism for cessation.

claim: This mechanism may provide a means to couple cessation of nephron formation with organ growth, invoking only a relatively simple set of niche behaviours.
source: This mechanism may provide a means to couple cessation of nephron formation with organ growth, invoking only a relatively simple set of niche behaviours.
evidence: Interpretation of the functional significance of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Cap mesenchyme cell cycle length, and hence proliferation rate, reduces with developmental time.
source: Observations that cap mesenchyme cell cycle length, and hence proliferation rate, reduces with developmental time (Short et al., 2014) and that cap populations represent a more committed state with time (Chen et al., 2015) are consistent with this model of stochastic commitment in a shrinking niche.
evidence: Statement of previous observations with citation.

claim: Around birth there is a simultaneous induction of nephrons all the way around the terminal ureteric tips with all remaining surrounding cells forming RVs.
source: Indeed, we have also previously shown in mouse that around birth there is a simultaneous induction of nephrons all the way around the terminal ureteric tips with all remaining surrounding cells forming RVs (Rumballe et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement of previous observation with citation.
